tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. import heapq, collections
def heap_general2(items, int_key):
    """items: list of (key_tuple, sym). Merge with heap; internal nodes get key (count,) + int_key(n)."""
    heap = [(k, (s,)) for k, s in items]
    heapq.heapify(heap)
    depth = {s: 0 for _, s in items}
    nxt = 0
    while len(heap) > 1:
        ka, a = heapq.heappop(heap)
        kb, b = heapq.heappop(heap)
        for s in a + b: depth[s] += 1
        nxt += 1
        heapq.heappush(heap, ((ka[0] + kb[0],) + int_key(nxt), a + b))
    return depth
def lim_variant(hist, limit, leafkey, int_key=lambda n: (-1, -n), step='double'):
    cl = 1
    while True:
        items = [((max(c, cl),) + leafkey(s, c), s) for s, c in hist.items()]
        d = heap_general2(items, int_key)
        if max(d.values()) <= limit: return d, cl
        cl = cl * 2 if step == 'double' else cl + 1
def package_merge(hist, L):
    syms = sorted(hist, key=lambda s: (hist[s], s))
    n = len(syms)
    # standard package-merge: lists of (weight, multiset of symbols)
    leaves = [(hist[s], [s]) for s in syms]
    cur = list(leaves)
    for _ in range(L - 1):
        pk = []
        for i in range(0, len(cur) - 1, 2):
            pk.append((cur[i][0] + cur[i+1][0], cur[i][1] + cur[i+1][1]))
        cur = sorted(leaves + pk, key=lambda x: x[0])
    sel = cur[:2 * n - 2]
    d = collections.Counter()
    for w, ss in sel:
        for s in ss: d[s] += 1
    return dict(d)
def scale_down(hist, limit, leafkey=lambda s, c: (0, -s), int_key=lambda n: (-1, -n), mode='halve'):
    h = dict(hist)
    while True:
        items = [((c,) + leafkey(s, c), s) for s, c in h.items()]
        d = heap_general2(items, int_key)
        if max(d.values()) <= limit: return d
        if mode == 'halve': h = {s: max(1, (c + 1) // 2) for s, c in h.items()}
        elif mode == 'halve_floor': h = {s: max(1, c // 2) for s, c in h.items()}
        elif mode == 'shift': h = {s: (c >> 1) | 1 for s, c in h.items()}

from br import *
cases = []
def C(name, bw): cases.append((name, bw.bytes()))
# uncompressed padding with real padding bits (wbits16 -> 21 bits header -> 3 pad bits)
for pad in (0, 1, 2, 4, 7):
    bw = BW(); wbits(bw, 16); uncompressed(bw, b'abc', pad=pad); last_empty(bw); C('unc_w16_pad%x' % pad, bw)
# metadata padding: various
for pad in (0, 1, 0x20):
    bw = BW(); wbits(bw, 16); metadata(bw, b'xyz', pad=pad); last_empty(bw); C('meta_w16_pad%x' % pad, bw)
# metadata skip0 with padding bits nonzero
bw = BW(); wbits(bw, 16); metadata(bw, b'', skipbytes=0, pad=1); last_empty(bw); C('meta_skip0_pad1', bw)
# 6 nibbles valid (mlen 2^20+1) uncompressed but truncated
bw = BW(); wbits(bw, 24); mb_header(bw, (1 << 20) + 1, uncompressed=True, nibbles=6); bw.align(); bw.put(0x61, 8); C('unc_nib6_valid_trunc', bw)
bw = BW(); wbits(bw, 24); mb_header(bw, (1 << 20) + 1, uncompressed=False, nibbles=6); C('cmp_nib6_valid_trunc', bw)
bw = BW(); wbits(bw, 24); mb_header(bw, (1 << 24), uncompressed=False, nibbles=6); C('cmp_nib6_max_trunc', bw)
# exuberant nibble and then EOF exactly at end of nibbles (no ISUNCOMPRESSED bit)
bw = BW(); wbits(bw, 16); bw.put(0, 1); bw.put(1, 2); bw.put(0, 20); bw.put(0, 1)  # 24 bits: w16(1) islast(1) mn(2) 20 nibble bits => 24 bits, no isunc
b = bw.bytes(); cases.append(('exub_nib5_eof_before_isunc', b[:3]))
bw = BW(); wbits(bw, 16); bw.put(0, 1); bw.put(1, 2); bw.put(0, 20)
cases.append(('exub_nib5_eof_before_isunc2', bw.bytes()))
# eof in the middle of nibbles
cases.append(('eof_mid_nibbles', bytes([0x00, 0x00])))
# reserved bit set and EOF right after
bw = BW(); wbits(bw, 22); bw.put(0, 1); bw.put(3, 2); bw.put(1, 1); cases.append(('meta_reserved_eof', bw.bytes()))
# exuberant metadata byte and EOF right after
bw = BW(); wbits(bw, 22); bw.put(0, 1); bw.put(3, 2); bw.put(0, 1); bw.put(2, 2); bw.put(5, 8); bw.put(0, 8); cases.append(('meta_exub_eof', bw.bytes()))
# metadata length larger than remaining input but nonzero padding
bw = BW(); wbits(bw, 16); metadata(bw, b'xyz', pad=1); b = bw.bytes()[:-1]; cases.append(('meta_pad1_overrun', b))
# metadata with padding bits nonzero AND EOF right at boundary
run_all(cases)

import json, sys, re, collections
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/agent_b')
from br import trace
cnt = collections.Counter()
for l in open(sys.argv[1]):
    c = json.loads(l)
    t = trace(bytes.fromhex(c['hex']))
    for m in re.finditer(r'HDR nbltypes L=(\d+) I=(\d+) D=(\d+) npostfix=(\d+) ndirect=(\d+) cmodes=\[([^\]]*)\] ntreesl=(\d+) ntreesd=(\d+)', t):
        L, I, D, pf, nd, cm, tl, td = m.groups()
        if int(L) > 1: cnt['nbltypesL>1'] += 1
        if int(I) > 1: cnt['nbltypesI>1'] += 1
        if int(D) > 1: cnt['nbltypesD>1'] += 1
        if int(pf): cnt['npostfix>0'] += 1
        if int(nd): cnt['ndirect>0'] += 1
        for x in cm.split(','):
            if x.strip(): cnt['cmode' + x.strip()] += 1
        if int(tl) > 1: cnt['ntreesl>1'] += 1
        if int(td) > 1: cnt['ntreesd>1'] += 1
    cnt['uncompressed_mb'] += t.count('uncompressed=true')
    cnt['complex_codes'] += t.count('COMPLEX hskip=0'); cnt['hskip2'] += t.count('COMPLEX hskip=2'); cnt['hskip3'] += t.count('COMPLEX hskip=3')
    for m in re.finditer(r'DIST code=(\d+) distance=(\d+) maxd=(\d+)', t):
        dc, d, md = map(int, m.groups())
        if d > md: cnt['dict_ref'] += 1
        if dc < 16: cnt['dcode<16'] += 1
    cnt['metadata'] += t.count('metadata')
    cnt['streams'] += 1
print(dict(cnt))

from enc import *

def rand_cmap(rng, n, ntrees):
    if ntrees == 1: return [0] * n
    mode = rng.random()
    if mode < 0.3: return [rng.randrange(ntrees) for _ in range(n)]
    if mode < 0.6:  # mostly zeros with runs
        return [0 if rng.random() < 0.8 else rng.randrange(ntrees) for _ in range(n)]
    # blocky
    out = []
    while len(out) < n:
        out += [rng.randrange(ntrees)] * rng.randint(1, 20)
    return out[:n]

def gen_mb(rng, st, islast, big=False):
    npostfix = rng.choice([0, 0, 1, 2, 3])
    ndirect = rng.choice([0, 0, rng.randint(0, 15)]) << npostfix
    nbl = [rng.choice([1, 1, 2, 3, rng.randint(2, 6)]) for _ in range(3)]
    if big and rng.random() < 0.3: nbl[rng.randrange(3)] = rng.choice([128, 255, 256])
    cmodes = [rng.randrange(4) for _ in range(nbl[0])]
    ntreesl = rng.choice([1, 1, 2, 3, rng.randint(1, 8)])
    ntreesd = rng.choice([1, 1, 2, rng.randint(1, 5)])
    cmapl = rand_cmap(rng, 64 * nbl[0], ntreesl)
    cmapd = rand_cmap(rng, 4 * nbl[2], ntreesd)
    cmapl_opts = dict(rlemax=rng.choice([0, 0, 1, 3, 6, 16]), imtf=rng.random() < 0.4)
    cmapd_opts = dict(rlemax=rng.choice([0, 0, 2, 5]), imtf=rng.random() < 0.4)
    # commands
    cmds = []
    ncmd = rng.randint(1, 12)
    # simulate to pick valid distances: need State copy
    sim = State(st.wbits); sim.out = bytearray(st.out); sim.rb = list(st.rb)
    produced = 0
    alphabet = rng.choice([b'abc', b'abcdefghij', bytes(range(256)), b'the quick brown fox ', b'\x00\x01\xff\x80'])
    for i in range(ncmd):
        ins = bytes(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(rng.choice([0, 1, 2, 5, rng.randint(0, 40)])))
        sim.out += ins; produced += len(ins)
        last = (i == ncmd - 1)
        if last and rng.random() < 0.3 and ins:
            cmds.append(dict(ins=ins, copy=4, dist=None))
            break
        md = sim.max_dist()
        r = rng.random()
        if md >= 1 and r < 0.65:
            cp = rng.choice([2, 3, 4, 5, rng.randint(2, 40), rng.randint(2, 300)])
            # prefer recent distances sometimes
            cands = [d for d in sim.rb if 1 <= d <= md]
            if cands and rng.random() < 0.4:
                d = rng.choice(cands) + rng.choice([0, 0, -1, 1, 2, -2, 3, -3])
                d = max(1, min(md, d))
            else:
                d = rng.randint(1, md)
            implicit = (d == sim.rb[0]) and rng.random() < 0.5
            cmds.append(dict(ins=ins, copy=cp, dist=None if implicit else d))
            for _ in range(cp): sim.out.append(sim.out[-d])
            produced += cp
            dc = 0 if implicit else sim.find_dcode(d, npostfix, ndirect)[0]
            if dc != 0: sim.rb = [d] + sim.rb[:3]
        else:
            # dictionary reference
            cp = rng.randint(4, 24)
            while True:
                idx = rng.randrange(1 << NDBITS[cp]); t = rng.randrange(121)
                w = transform(dict_word(cp, idx), t)
                if len(w) > 0: break
            d = md + 1 + (idx | (t << NDBITS[cp]))
            cmds.append(dict(ins=ins, copy=cp, dist=d))
            sim.out += w; produced += len(w)
    mlen = produced
    if mlen == 0:
        cmds = [dict(ins=b'z', copy=4, dist=None)]; mlen = 1
    # blocks: counts per category from symbol usage is complicated -> random splits with large final block
    def rand_blocks(n):
        if n == 1: return None
        bl = [(0, rng.randint(1, 6))]
        prev = [1, 0]
        for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 8)):
            bl.append((rng.randrange(n), rng.randint(1, 6)))
        bl.append((rng.randrange(n), 1 << 20))
        return bl
    blocks = tuple(rand_blocks(n) for n in nbl)
    compressed_mb(bw_holder[0], st, mlen, cmds, islast=islast, nbl=tuple(nbl), blocks=blocks, npostfix=npostfix, ndirect=ndirect,
                  cmodes=cmodes, ntreesl=ntreesl, cmapl=cmapl, cmapl_opts=cmapl_opts, ntreesd=ntreesd, cmapd=cmapd,
                  cmapd_opts=cmapd_opts)

bw_holder = [None]
def gen_stream(rng):
    w = rng.choice([10, 11, 12, 16, 17, 18, 22, 24])
    bw, st = new_stream(w)
    bw_holder[0] = bw
    nmb = rng.randint(1, 4)
    for i in range(nmb):
        last = (i == nmb - 1)
        r = rng.random()
        if r < 0.12 and not last:
            data = bytes(rng.randrange(256) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 30)))
            uncompressed(bw, data); st.out += data
        elif r < 0.2 and not last:
            metadata(bw, bytes(rng.randrange(256) for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 10))))
        else:
            gen_mb(rng, st, islast=last and rng.random() < 0.7, big=rng.random() < 0.2)
    if not last or True:
        # if last generated block wasn't islast, close stream
        pass
    return bw, st

if __name__ == '__main__':
    seed0 = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 1
    n = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 100
    cases = []; expects = []
    for k in range(n):
        rng = random.Random(seed0 * 100000 + k)
        bw, st = gen_stream(rng)
        # ensure termination: append last-empty if needed (harmless if a previous islast exists? no -> check bits)
        b = bw.bytes()
        # we can't easily know whether last mb was islast; decode with ref to see; else append last_empty
        r = run_ref(b)
        if not r['ok']:

        cases.append(('fuzz_%d_%d' % (seed0, k), b)); expects.append(bytes(st.out))
    o = run_orig(cases); nd = run_node(cases)
    bad = 0

        okn = rn['ok'] and rn['out_hex'] == ex.hex()
        oko = ro['ok'] and ro['out_hex'] == ex.hex()
        if not (okn and oko):
            bad += 1
            print(name, 'len', len(b), 'node', fmt(rn, 40), '| orig', fmt(ro, 40), '| expected len', len(ex))
    print('done', n, 'bad', bad)

from br import *
def sweep(name, comp, inp, step=1, maxcases=None):
    cases = [('%s_trunc%d' % (name, n), comp[:n]) for n in range(0, len(comp) + 1, step)]
    # batch so that json < 900KB

    batch = []; size = 0
    def flush():

        if batch:

    for c in cases:
        s = len(c[1]) * 2 + 100
        if size + s > 400000: flush()
        batch.append(c); size += s
    flush()
    runs = []  # (start, end, msg) run-length summary
    for (nm, b), ro, rn in zip(cases, res_o, res_n):
        if ro['ok']:
            m = 'OK' + ('(full)' if ro['out_hex'] == inp.hex() else '(partial %d)' % (len(ro['out_hex']) // 2))
        else:

        mn = 'OK' if rn['ok'] else rn['message'] + ('/' + rn.get('code', '') if rn.get('code') else '')

}

    """records for big outputs lack out_hex -> regenerate from reference decoder and verify len/fnv"""
    if o.get('ok') and 'out_hex' not in o:
        r = run_ref(bytes.fromhex(hx))
        assert r['ok'], name
        out = bytes.fromhex(r['out_hex'])
        h = 2166136261
        for x in out:

        assert len(out) == o['out_len'] and h == o['out_fnv'], (name, len(out), o)
        return {'ok': True, 'out_hex': r['out_hex']}

import collections

138	    - Ex: "1b00000020c202bf807e4fff01" (vs "...7c4fff01" = 2^24 gives mismatch).
139	RangeError "Invalid typed array length"  (not a brotli message)
140	    Decode succeeded but output > 1,048,576 bytes. This is the runtime's 1 MiB cap on any
141	    TypedArray/Buffer; fs.readFileSync of > 1 MiB fails the same way.
142	    - The decoder itself is not limited: a brotli error found after > 1 MiB of output still wins.
143	    - Exactly 1 MiB is OK.
144	    - Ex: "9f0000100020c2e2b18074ef1f00" (1 MiB + 1). Valid 6-nibble meta-blocks always hit this.
145	
146	2. PARSE ORDER (first failing check wins; everything is sequential, deferred checks as noted)
147	--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
148	Stream header:
149	  WBITS (marker -> large-window error).
150	Meta-block header, loop:
151	  ISLAST; [ISLASTEMPTY -> stream ends]; MNIBBLES.
152	  Metadata branch:
153	    reserved -> MSKIPBYTES -> bytes -> exuberant byte -> padding -> overrun -> skip.
154	    If ISLAST, end.
155	  Data branch:
156	    nibbles -> exuberant -> [ISUNCOMPRESSED if !ISLAST].
157	    Uncompressed: padding -> overrun -> copy.
158	Compressed header (RFC order):
159	  NBLTYPES/btype code/bcount code/first count for L, I, D -> NPOSTFIX, NDIRECT -> cmodes ->
160	  NTREESL + cmap -> NTREESD + cmap -> literal, command and distance codes.
161	Commands until remaining <= 0:
162	  [I switch] -> cmd symbol + insert/copy extra -> literals (each with [L switch]) ->
163	  [insert MLEN check] -> [stop if done] -> distance (implicit, or [D switch] + symbol + extra) ->
164	  short-distance check -> dict(len, transform) or copy -> MLEN check.
165	Semantics all confirmed equal to node on valid data:
166	  - Window rule max_distance = min(pos, 2^WBITS-16) holds (WBITS=10: d=1008 copies, d=1009 is a
167	    dictionary word).
168	  - Dictionary refs and code 0 do not update the distance ring buffer.
169	  - Block-type ring buffer starts at (1,0); sym0 = second-to-last, sym1 = last+1 mod N, else sym-2.
170	  - All 26 block-count codes.
171	  - NBLTYPES 1..256 (varlen8 caps at 256; >256 is not encodable).
172	  - NTREES up to 256; RLEMAX 1..16 and IMTF.
173	  - Context modes 0..3 (MSB6 too, which node never emits).
174	  - NPOSTFIX 0..3 and NDIRECT up to 120.
175	  - Zero-length transformed words are accepted.
176	
177	3. EOF / TRUNCATION SUMMARY
178	--------------------------
179	Node streams q5/q11 (one meta-block, 344..7059 B) and flush-built 5-meta-block streams (490/497 B,
180	including an uncompressed block) were cut at every length.
181	- Every prefix gives "unexpected end of input".
182	- Exception: prefixes that end inside an uncompressed block's payload, with the header complete
183	  and 0..MLEN-1 payload bytes present, give "uncompressed block overruns input". Full length gives OK.
184	- 29k prefixes of 250 crafted valid vectors gave only those two messages, plus "metadata overruns
185	  input" inside metadata payloads. OK only appeared when nothing but trailing garbage was removed.
186	
187	4. LAX BEHAVIOURS / DIFFERENCES FROM NODE
188	----------------------------------------
189	- Final padding is NOT checked (node: ERR__ERROR_FORMAT_PADDING_2). This covers the bits after
190	  ISLAST+ISLASTEMPTY and after a compressed ISLAST block.
191	  - "deadbeef" -> OK empty. Also "fb" -> OK, "81ff" -> OK.
192	  - Example "1b040000a0cbd0d8de040a01488d" -> "hello".
193	- Trailing bytes after the stream end are ignored (node too).
194	- Otherwise exactly as strict as node: in 100k differential mutated streams there was no
195	  orig-OK/node-fail except PADDING_2, no orig-fail/node-OK, and no differing output.
196	- Message mapping to node codes:
197	  - CL_SPACE -> corrupt code-length code
198	  - HUFFMAN_SPACE -> under/over-subscribed, or run overflows alphabet for repeat overflow
199	  - BLOCK_LENGTH_1/2 -> meta-block length mismatch (or EOF, since literals are read first)
200	  - DISTANCE -> invalid short distance
201	  - DICTIONARY -> invalid dictionary reference length
202	  - TRANSFORM -> invalid dictionary transform
203	  - CONTEXT_MAP_REPEAT -> context map run overflows
204	  - PADDING_1 -> non-zero padding bits
205	  - RESERVED -> reserved bit set
206	  - EXUBERANT_NIBBLE / EXUBERANT_META_NIBBLE -> exuberant size nibble / metadata size byte
207	  - SIMPLE_HUFFMAN_ALPHABET / SAME -> out of range / duplicate
208	  - WINDOW_BITS -> large-window
209	  - Z_BUF_ERROR -> unexpected end of input, or the two overrun messages
210	- Order differences from node:
211	  - Insert overrun: node fails before reading literals.
212	  - Over-subscribed code: orig fails at once, node reads on (often EOF).
213	
214	5. VALID-STREAM CONFORMANCE
215	--------------------------
216	Every set matched byte-for-byte:
217	- 1880 node streams: q0..11, lgwin 10..24, modes 0..2, 12 inputs (0 B..40 KB).
218	- 69 large node streams up to 1 MiB output: LGBLOCK, NPOSTFIX/NDIRECT, disabled literal context modeling.
219	- 3150 random crafted valid streams: all header features, dictionary refs with all transforms,
220	  windows 10..24, mixed metadata/uncompressed/compressed blocks.
221	- An exhaustive set: 121 transforms x lengths 4..24 x 3 words.
222	
223	6. INPUT ARG (side note)
224	------------------------
225	- Input is converted like Buffer.from: strings as UTF-8; arrays and ArrayBuffer are accepted.
226	- A DataView decodes as empty input (gives "unexpected end of input").
227	- Number, null or undefined -> TypeError "Buffer.from: unsupported value".

content.text:
I found 19 distinct brotli error messages plus one runtime `RangeError`, and mapped the trigger and check order for each. The decoder is as strict as node except for one lax behaviour: it never checks the final padding bits after the last meta-block.

**Deliverables**
- **`/tmp/agent_b/cases.json`**: 1021 vectors as `{name, hex, orig}`, all re-run against `/tmp/orig` with no mismatches. Inputs are at most 1.4 KB. The file is 2.7 MB because one OK case has a 1 MiB output. The `RangeError` cases also carry `"error_type": "RangeError"`.
- **`/tmp/agent_b/REPORT.txt`**: the full catalog below, with a node error-code mapping and an example hex per message.
- **Tools**: crafting libraries `/tmp/agent_b/br.py` and `/tmp/agent_b/enc.py`; batch runner `/tmp/agent_b/runner.js`, which works under both orig and node.

**Error object.** Every error is a plain `Error` whose message starts with `"brotli: "`. Its only own property is `message` (no stack, code or errno).

**Messages and triggers**

| Message | Trigger, and when it is checked |
|---|---|
| `brotli: unexpected end of input` | Any read that needs a bit past the end, raised at that read. Missing bits are never treated as zero. Empty input gives this. Huffman look-ahead past the end is safe; it only fails if the actual codeword is longer than the bits left. |
| `brotli: uncompressed block overruns input` | MLEN is larger than the whole bytes left, checked before copying (also when 0 bytes are left). |
| `brotli: metadata overruns input` | MSKIPLEN is larger than the bytes left. |
| `brotli: large-window streams are not supported` | WBITS pattern `0010001`, raised immediately whatever follows (even end of input). Every other WBITS pattern is valid. |
| `brotli: exuberant size nibble` | MNIBBLES is 5 or 6 and the top nibble is 0. Checked before ISUNCOMPRESSED is read. |
| `brotli: reserved bit set` | Metadata reserved bit is 1. |
| `brotli: exuberant metadata size byte` | MSKIPBYTES ≥ 2 and the top MSKIPLEN byte is 0. Checked before the padding. |
| `brotli: non-zero padding bits` | Fill bits before metadata data (even with MSKIPBYTES=0) or before uncompressed data are not zero. |
| `brotli: simple code symbol out of range` | Simple-code symbol ≥ alphabet size, checked as each symbol is read. |
| `brotli: duplicate simple code symbol` | Checked only after all symbols are read and range-checked, before the tree-select bit. |
| `brotli: corrupt code-length code` | The code-length-code lengths are over-full (fails immediately) or not full after all entries are read. Exactly one non-zero length is accepted and becomes a 0-bit code. |
| `brotli: code-length run overflows alphabet` | A 16/17 repeat would go past the alphabet end. This beats the over-subscription check. |
| `brotli: prefix code is under/over-subscribed` | Over-subscription fails immediately (node reads on and often reports end of input). Also raised if the alphabet runs out with the code incomplete, including all-zero and single-symbol complex codes. |
| `brotli: context map run overflows` | An RLE zero-run would pass the end of the map. |
| `brotli: meta-block length mismatch` | Insert overrun: all literals are decoded first, then this error, with no distance read; truncated literals give end of input (node fails before reading them). Copy overrun: checked after the distance is read and validated, using the transformed length for dictionary words. |
| `brotli: invalid short distance` | Distance codes 4..15 give a distance ≤ 0. |
| `brotli: invalid dictionary reference length` | Distance > min(output so far, 2^WBITS−16) with copy length outside 4..24. |
| `brotli: invalid dictionary transform` | Transform index ≥ 121. |
| `brotli: block length exhausted with a single block type` | With NBLTYPES=1 the block length is an implicit 2^24 per meta-block. Needing literal 2^24+1 raises this; it is only reachable through an insert overrun. |
| `RangeError "Invalid typed array length"` | Successful decode with output over 1,048,576 bytes. This is the runtime's general 1 MiB buffer cap (`readFileSync` fails the same way). Exactly 1 MiB is OK, and a brotli error found later still wins. |

**Check order.** Everything is parsed sequentially and the first failing check wins. Meta-block header:
- Metadata: reserved bit → MSKIPBYTES → size bytes → exuberant-byte check → padding → overrun.
- Data: nibbles → exuberant check → ISUNCOMPRESSED → padding → overrun.

For each distance, the checks run in this order: short-distance check → dictionary length → dictionary transform → MLEN check.

**Lax behaviours and other differences from node**
- Final padding after ISLAST+ISLASTEMPTY or after the last compressed block is not checked. `deadbeef`, `fb` and `81ff` all decode to empty; node rejects them with PADDING_2.
- Trailing bytes after the stream end are ignored (node does the same).
- Across 100k bit-mutated streams run through both, padding was the only case where orig accepted and node rejected. There were no cases the other way round and no differing outputs.

**Valid streams.** Everything decoded byte-identical to node:
- 1880 node streams: quality 0..11, lgwin 10..24, modes 0..2.
- 69 large node streams up to 1 MiB, with LGBLOCK, NPOSTFIX/NDIRECT and context modelling off.
- 3150 random crafted streams covering every feature.
- All 121 dictionary transforms at every word length 4..24.

**Truncation.** I cut node quality-5 and quality-11 streams, including 5-meta-block streams, at every byte length. Every prefix gives `unexpected end of input`. The exceptions are prefixes ending inside an uncompressed block's data, which give `uncompressed block overruns input`, and inside metadata data, which give `metadata overruns input`.

**Input handling (side note).** Input is converted like `Buffer.from`: strings as UTF-8, arrays and ArrayBuffers are accepted. A DataView is treated as empty. Numbers, null and undefined throw a TypeError.
